beyond: The record commits to a specific judging design the owner never described: JEV answers first above a calibrated threshold, a configured judge model answers below it, a judge_model setting governs all verdicts, and the key stays out of the repository. The owner only said the system shouldn't rely on deterministic tooling to understand intent or process text unless a deterministic solution is sure to handle every case, and that intent recording needs deeper brainstorming.

"Every record the agent writes or changes is checked by a judge independent of the coding agent... JEV answers first when it is confident past the threshold calibrated on your own answers; otherwise the judge model you configured answers" adds a verification architecture the owner did not ask for.

The "will:" commitments (judge every stale link from any checkout, log which judge gave each verdict and its confidence, never fast-track on a quote, say once when no judge is reachable and hold only steps needing a verdict) are new behaviour and rules. The owner's words ask a question about the best UX for recording intent, so the record turns an open brainstorming question into settled decisions.
